title: Pneumatic — Bleed Overheat Sensor — Relocation and Installation of the Revised Pre-Cooler Outlet Duct
abstract: Relocation of the bleed overheat sensor clear of the pre-cooler elbow radiant field, together with a revised outlet duct, to remove the nuisance bleed leak warnings that shut a bleed system down in the climb.

sections.planning_reason: Nuisance bleed leak warnings in the climb produced one hundred and thirty in-flight bleed shutdowns in 2017 and 2018 across the tracked fleet, and none was followed by a confirmed duct leak on the ground. Instrumented flights showed the overheat sensor seeing radiant heat from the pre-cooler outlet elbow rather than air temperature, with the effect growing with outside air temperature at top of climb. Operators lose a bleed system on about one flight in four hundred, with the single-pack cabin and the dispatch penalty that follows an unexplained shutdown.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin installs a revised pre-cooler outlet duct with a longer straight run before the first bend, and relocates the overheat sensor two hundred and forty millimetres outboard onto a new bracket clear of the elbow radiant field. The isolation valve is retained with a shortened actuating rod to suit the new duct geometry. The bracket is bolted into existing pylon hard points and no new hole is drilled in primary structure.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make sure that the engine is cool and that the bleed system is depressurised. Open the fan cowls and remove the pylon lower fairing to get access to zones 431, 433 and 443. Disconnect the sensor harness at the existing position. Remove the pre-cooler outlet duct and install the pipe ES695992-47 with new joint seals. Install the sensor bracket with the bolts LN212801K2 into the existing hard points and check the torque. Install the sensor D3610116027716 on the new bracket and route the harness clear of the duct. Shorten the actuating rod of the isolation valve D3610114004535 to the dimension in the instructions and re-rig it. Check that the filter PE873965-99 upstream of the valve is undisturbed and that the regulator at FIN 16PU has not moved. Do a bleed system leak check at operating pressure. Do the bleed leak detection loop test following task AMM-Z-36-10-11-200-032-A. Repeat for the second engine and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable per engine to aircraft in the MSN Z02497 to Z09175 range with VDK-56B or VNT-2500A engines. One stored aircraft is excluded. Aircraft delivered from the production cut-in already have the revised duct and sensor position.
sections.material_note: Kit K3610-1009-01 covers one engine and contains the outlet duct, the sensor bracket, the bolt set, the joint seals and the shortened actuating rod. Two kits are required per aircraft. The duct is a sixteen week item.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 24 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, or at the next engine removal, whichever occurs first.
